claim: Divides the frame so three reactions can land at once, which is something frame-in-frame cannot do. Diagonal shards are the shock version, manga panels are the stylised one, and inset PiP is how you keep a face on screen while showing what it is looking at.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: diagonal shard panels, shattered split screen
inset panel, small picture in picture corner panel
manga panels, comic page layout, panel gutters
radial wedge panels, pie sliced split screen

review.issue: two_v / two_h / three_v / grid_4 depend on the model counting panels, which it does not do reliably from phrases like "three vertical panels" - "split screen" is barely a tag. two_v and three_v in particular will be indistinguishable.
review.fix: Use the danbooru tags that actually encode panel layout: two_v/two_h -> "2koma", grid_4 -> "4koma", manga_panels -> "comic, panel layout", inset_pip -> "inset". Drop three_v, which has no tag and no reliable count.

look_at: manga_panels and two_v read; grid_4 and inset_pip never divide the frame.
